chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza, Hamza, who said:

I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: 'Wonder upon wonder for the one who denies death while he sees people dying every day and night; and wonder upon wonder for the one who denies the next creation while he observes the first creation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the paradox of denying death and resurrection according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) critiques the cognitive dissonance of humanity, who accept the reality of the first creation (al-nash'a al-ula) yet reject the certainty of the hereafter (al-nash'a al-ukhra). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'tadabbur' (deep reflection) upon natural signs as a prerequisite for faith, linking empirical observation directly to theological conviction.
